subject: EXCLUSIVE Hand Drawn Stickers By SKEME
bio_paragraph_1: Born John Cecil Dash in Harlem in 1964, SKEME began writing graffiti on New York City’s subway system at 15, quickly becoming an “All City” writer. He painted across numerous subway lines and collaborated with some of the era’s most influential graffiti artists, creating iconic pieces and mastering everything from wildstyle and whole cars to throw-ups and handstyles.
bio_paragraph_2: In 1982, SKEME was featured alongside his mother in the groundbreaking documentary Style Wars, helping introduce New York graffiti and hip-hop culture to a worldwide audience.
bio_paragraph_3: His legacy goes beyond the film. SKEME collaborated with legendary pioneer PHASE 2 on the historic TUFF CITY train, alongside artists including Tean, Kade, Chains3, Kool131 and Part1. The project earned him membership in TMT (The Magnificent Team), one of graffiti’s most respected crews of the era.

subject: From Graffiti to Fashion: Shirt King Phade Exclusive Collection
bio_paragraph_1: Shirt King Phade (Edwin "Phade" Sacasa) is a pioneering New York graffiti artist who helped transform graffiti into wearable art during the early days of hip-hop. After moving from painting subway trains to customizing airbrushed T-shirts, Phade and the Shirt Kings became among the first artists to commercialize graffiti, laying the foundation for what many consider modern streetwear. Known for his bold, hand-painted designs that remixed pop culture icons with hip-hop style, the Shirt Kings' custom apparel became a cultural phenomenon. His iconic Queens storefront attracted hip-hop legends including Jay-Z, Jam Master Jay, and RZA, helping shape some of the era's most recognizable imagery.

subject: Meet COCO144: New Limited-Edition Releases Are Here
bio_paragraph_1: Roberto Gualtieri, known as COCO144, is an artist and pioneer among the first generation of New York City subway writers. His tag was inspired by his childhood nickname and the street in Harlem where he grew up, 144th Street.
bio_paragraph_2: In November 1972, COCO144 was one of the founding members of United Graffiti Artists, a collective of artists who revolutionized the writing movement and changed the public's perception of urban art by transitioning from spray painting on subway trains to painting on canvas.

subject: August T-Shirt Drop: YUBIA is Live
artist_bio: Yubia is a graffiti writer, muralist, and illustrator from Bilbao, Spain, currently based in Barcelona. Active in the graffiti scene since 2002, she has developed a distinctive visual language that blends classic graffiti lettering with playful kawaii-inspired characters, bold color palettes, and contemporary pop culture references. Her work transforms everyday objects, food, spray cans, and urban elements into expressive characters that bring humor, optimism, and energy to walls around the world.

subject: Exclusive T-Shirt Drop: SONIC Is Live
artist_bio: Jesse Rodriguez, born and raised in New York City, found his artistic calling in graffiti during the early 1970s. Sonic pioneered unique graffiti styles, introducing 3D folding letters and transforming letters into characters, leaving an indelible mark on Hip Hop culture. Painting NYC subway trains posed numerous challenges for Sonic: from stealing spray paint to navigating the city’s dangers en route to train yards, the process involved sneaking in and facing constant police pursuits. Despite these obstacles, Sonic’s determination and passion for his craft drove him to leave a lasting imprint on the subway cars, contributing to the vibrant and rebellious culture of graffiti in the 1970s and beyond. Notable works like “Revolution 81” and “World War III” on NYC subway cars showcase his influence.
